description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2022: Efficient supercomputer resource utilization for machine learning: a case study on identifying damage in a five-story reinforced concrete structure is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Claudia Marin, Howard University (howard.edu). In this poster, presented at the NHERI Natural Hazards Summit 2022, we present an efficient approach for high-performance computing (HPC) resource utilization for machine learning (ML). Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-qxz0-8n72. Keywords: Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC); high-performance computing (HPC); machine learning; transfer learning; damage identification; reinforced concrete structures. Published 2023-04-06. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
